text:
elena: quick follow-up from today's gateway sync — I want to propose a lightweight preemptive stream priority mechanism that only interrupts streams at clearly defined safepoints instead of mid-chunk. goal: reduce tail latency for high-priority traffic without corrupting partial responses.

sam: sounds promising. can you define what you mean by safepoint? is it token boundary, user-provided commit, or something runtime-detected?

elena: short answer: runtime-detected *and* opt-in checkpoints. 2 things: (1) runtime emits 'safepoint' when output is on a logical boundary (e.g., end of message or after emit flush), (2) client can opt into explicit safepoints via a header when their app can resume from a checkpoint.

kevin: important distinction: many models stream partial natural language; we shouldn't require model changes. runtime heuristics (newline, punctuation, EOS logits) could approximate safepoints. but we need a clear contract for data-loss semantics.

elena: exactly. proposal for contract: preemption can only happen at safepoints. when preempted, edge sends a short 2xx-with-status frame to client indicating ephemeral preempt + preemption-id. that id maps to a 30s retry window we keep in the control-plane cache. clients can retry to continue from the safepoint by including Preempt-Id header.

matt: two quick tradeoffs: (A) keeping retry state in control plane adds memory and auth considerations; (B) exposing Preempt-Id means we must validate tenant and auth on resume. both manageable but call out in design.

elena: agreed. sketch for headers/payload:
```
Request: X-Stream-Priority: 20
         X-Stream-Safepoints: enabled
Response preempt: HTTP/1.1 204 Preempted
                  X-Preempt-Id: pmt-abc123
                  Retry-Window: 30
```

kevin: love the simplicity. question: how do we treat non-idempotent ops (tool calls, side-effects)? my thought: default to "no preempt" unless client explicitly marks op as resumable. we should also add a server-side policy: if request touches side-effect endpoints, block preempt.

elena: yes. default-deny for side-effects. we'll add a small annotation in our API catalog and runtime will check route metadata before allowing preemptive eviction.

sam: observability notes: please include spans/traces for safepoint emits and preempt events. we need token-level cost reporting for preempted requests (to avoid double billing on retries). also emit metric: preempt.count by priority and route.

elena: good call. I'll add metrics and a quick dashboard template. also adding an audit entry per Preempt-Id to satisfy compliance teams.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: edge/ingress v5.8.3 (canary) will include safepoint markers and metric hooks.

matt: follow-up action items: elena to write short RFC (1-2 pages) that defines safepoint heuristics, header contract, control-plane state TTL, and auth checks. kevin to prototype runtime heuristics. sam to add observability gaps. i'll scope mem/cost impact for cache entries.

elena: thanks — I'll drop the RFC into /doc/rfcs and ping here when ready. ping @sam @kevin for review. :thumbsup:
